overview: This file traces a dispute over whether non-Japanese vessels—especially Chinese-flag ships chartered to carry Texas Company petroleum products—could trade between Dairen in the Kwantung Leased Territory and ports in Japanese-ruled Korea. A December 1935 consular despatch and translated Japanese administrative correspondence argue that voyages between the leased territory and the Japanese Empire were not legally coastwise trade under the 1906 rules, while Korean customs officials nevertheless delayed cargoes and advised the company to use Japanese vessels. A Department of State memorandum considers the legal status of Kwantung after the creation of Manchukuo and concludes that discrimination against Chinese vessels alone would not warrant U.S. representations. A February 1936 follow-up records temporary Korean “toleration” of another Chinese-flag shipment, and later cross-reference sheets point to May 1936 reports concerning further investigation by Japan’s Foreign Ministry.

subfiles.title: Despatch on the exclusion of foreign vessels from Dairen–Korea trade
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, American Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Korean restrictions affecting Chinese vessels chartered by the Texas Company to carry petroleum products from Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The S.S. YUNG SAI carried petroleum products from Dairen to Shingishu, Chinampo, and subsequently Fusan, but Korean officials delayed or questioned discharge on the ground that foreign ships could not conduct this trade. Grummon argues that Imperial Ordinance No. 236 of August 31, 1906, and later administrative interpretations treated such voyages as outside Japanese coasting trade. After consulting the Texas Company and Kwantung officials, he reports that the Kwantung Foreign Affairs Section has requested an explanation from the Korean Government and that the company is awaiting instructions from Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Marine Affairs Bureau ruling to the Texas Company
subfiles.from: Chief of the Marine Affairs Bureau, Dairen
subfiles.about: States that foreign-vessel transportation between Dairen and Korea will not be treated as coastwise trade.
subfiles.summary: The bureau advises the Texas Company that it will treat the proposed foreign-vessel service as outside the coasting trade. It cites an August 1906 notice from the Japanese Foreign Minister and a notice to the Chief of the Kwantung Government attributed here to November 1925.

subfiles.title: Komura letter on foreign navigation between Dairen and Japan
subfiles.from: Marquis Kin’ichi Komura, Vice Minister of the Colonial Department
subfiles.to: Masahiro Ota, Chief of the Kwantung Government
subfiles.about: Directs the Kwantung Government to permit foreign vessels to carry passengers and cargo between Dairen and Japan without special permission pending a final policy.
subfiles.summary: Komura directs Ota to follow the Japanese Foreign Minister’s August 1906 notice governing navigation between Dairen and Japan and its territories. Referring to the Chinese ship Chukago, he reports that the Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs has been consulted and that foreign vessels should meanwhile be allowed to transport passengers and cargo without special permission. He adds that the chiefs of customs houses nationwide agreed with this interpretation.

subfiles.title: Heading on vessels between the Japanese Empire and Kwantung
subfiles.about: Identifies an enclosure concerning vessels navigating between the Japanese Empire and the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The page contains only the heading “MATTER CONCERNING VESSELS NAVIGATING BETWEEN JAPANESE EMPIRE AND KWANTUNG LEASED TERRITORY.” It apparently introduces or labels legal material associated with the preceding translated correspondence.

subfiles.title: Department memorandum on the Dairen–Korea carrying trade
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Analyzes the legal and diplomatic implications of excluding foreign vessels from trade between Dairen and Korean ports.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum summarizes the delays imposed on Chinese vessels carrying Texas Company petroleum and notes that the Korean Government has been asked for a ruling. It interprets Imperial Ordinance No. 236 as permitting foreign merchant vessels to navigate between the Japanese Empire and Kwantung. If Japan reclassified the voyages as coastwise trade, the United States might argue that leased Kwantung was not Japanese territory, although that position would require study of treaties and Kwantung’s status after Manchukuo’s creation. The memorandum concludes that interference with Chinese ships chartered by American companies would not by itself justify U.S. representations.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Grummon’s February 18 despatch
subfiles.about: Points to another file entry concerning whether Korean customs officials’ advice to the Texas Company was final.
subfiles.summary: The sheet directs researchers to file 895.801/2 for a February 18 despatch from Grummon at Dairen. It identifies the subject as the exclusion of foreign vessels from Dairen–Korea coastwise trade and the Texas Company’s inquiry about the finality of Korean customs officials’ advice.

subfiles.title: Despatch on temporary toleration of the S.S. PEI HAI shipment
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports arrangements for a Chinese-flag petroleum shipment to Incheon and asks whether Korea’s preference for Japanese vessels is final.
subfiles.summary: Grummon reports that the Texas Company arranged with the Japanese firm Matsuura Kaisen Kabushiki Kaisha to send cargo from Dairen to Jinsen aboard the Chinese-flag S.S. PEI HAI. The firm claimed to have secured Korean authorities’ “toleration” for this single shipment, expected to depart on February 19 or 20. Because the company wanted to continue using Chinese ships and anticipated another shipment around March 1, it sought clarification about whether Korean customs officials’ advice to use Japanese vessels was definitive.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Edson’s report on Dairen–Chosen trade
subfiles.about: Points to a Seoul report describing developments in the exclusion of non-Japanese vessels from Dairen–Chosen trade.
subfiles.summary: The sheet directs researchers to file 895.801/3 for Edson’s May 7 report from Seoul. The referenced report concerned new developments in the exclusion of non-Japanese vessels from the Dairen–Chosen coasting trade.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Grew’s report of a Foreign Ministry investigation
subfiles.about: Records that Japan’s Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs promised to investigate the Dairen–Chosen shipping restrictions.
subfiles.summary: The sheet directs researchers to file 895.801/4 for Grew’s May 13 report from Japan. It states that the Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs had promised to investigate the situation described in Seoul’s voluntary report of May 7.

interest: The file is especially useful for showing how an apparently narrow corporate shipping problem exposed unresolved questions about sovereignty, cabotage, and the legal status of Japan’s leased territory after the establishment of Manchukuo. It juxtaposes port-level enforcement, earlier Japanese administrative rulings, an American company’s petroleum logistics, and the State Department’s cautious assessment of when commercial inconvenience justified diplomatic intervention. The cross-reference sheets are also valuable archival evidence: they trace the controversy into related 895.801 files and document a later promise of investigation by Japan’s Foreign Ministry.
